The test image shows a corn ear with dark blue-green to gray-green fuzzy mold covering kernels. This is a seed/ear disease. Top candidates: Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, and possibly others.

Let me view references one at a time, starting with the top candidates.
Very similar - dark blue-green mold on kernels. Now let me check Aspergillus_Ear_Rot for comparison.
Aspergillus is olive-green/yellowish, much lighter than the test image. Let me check other seed/ear candidates.
Fusarium is whitish-pink mold - not a match. Let me check Gibberella.
Gibberella shows red/pink mold at ear tip - not a match. Let me check Diplodia_Ear_Rot.
Not a match - Diplodia shows white mycelium and grayish-brown discoloration. Let me check Head_Smut and Common_Smut.
Not a match - Head_Smut shows dark spore masses replacing the ear. Let me check Common_Smut on seed.
Not a match - Common_Smut shows distinctive silvery-white galls. Now let me view one more Trichoderma reference to confirm.

This shows dark blue-green conidia on husk leaves, consistent with Trichoderma.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Corn ear with dark blue-green fuzzy mold growing on and between kernels, covering most of the ear surface. Kernels are yellow/orange underneath.
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot reference (Corn_Disease_26.jpg)**: Nearly identical - same dark blue-green mold on and between yellow kernels, same distribution pattern.
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Much lighter olive-green/yellowish powdery mold - doesn't match.
- **Fusarium**: White/pink mold - no match.
- **Gibberella**: Red/pink mold at tip - no match.
- **Diplodia, Head_Smut, Common_Smut**: Completely different morphologies.

The KB description for Trichoderma confirms: "Dark blue-green layers of conidia on and between kernels; white mycelium on husk leaves turning green to gray-green." This matches perfectly.
